newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabena traffic up 10% in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabena traffic up 10% in Jan.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena recorded a 10 percent increase in traffic in January 1997 compared to the year-ago month, chief executive officer Paul Reutlinger said in a Belgian newspaper interview.
"We are delighted and this shows we are moving in the right direction as far as results are concerned," he told Le Soir.
He said that last December sales in Belgium had increased by 19 percent compared to December 1995, though he noted that the year-ago month had been troubled by strikes.
Reutlinger added that for the first time Sabena was first among European airlines in December in terms of punctuality.

Recognised by Belgium's Labour Ministry as a company in difficulty, Sabena had 1995 group loss of 530 million Belgian francs before provisions and a worse-than-expected two billion franc loss in the first-half of 1996.
Reutlinger repeated that the company expected a loss for 1997, though less than the loss for 1996, and that it should return to a "balanced budget" in 1998.
Sabena is 49.5 percent owned by Swissair.
